lines.name: Advance Variation
lines.intro: In the Advance, White pushes e5 to grab space. Your plan: get the light-squared bishop out to f5, then play ...e6 and hit White's pawn chain with ...c5.

notes.0: White opens with the king's pawn.
notes.1: ...c6 prepares ...d5 and keeps the c8 bishop's diagonal open.
notes.4: This is the Advance: White pushes past your pawn to gain space.
notes.5: The point of the Caro-Kann: the bishop gets out before ...e6 locks it in.
notes.6: White develops calmly and supports d4.
notes.7: Now ...e6 is fine. The light-squared bishop is already outside the pawn chain.
notes.9: ...c5 hits the base of White's d4–e5 chain.
notes.10: White defends d4 with the bishop. Keep up the pressure on d4 with ...Nc6 and ...Qb6 next.

lines.name: Exchange Variation
lines.intro: In the Exchange, White trades on d5 for a symmetrical pawn structure. You develop quickly, use the half-open c-file, and get your bishop out to g4 before playing ...e6.

notes.0: White opens with the king's pawn.
notes.1: ...c6 prepares ...d5 and keeps the c8 bishop's diagonal open.
notes.4: This is the Exchange: White trades pawns on d5.
notes.5: Take back with the c-pawn. The structure is symmetrical, but you get the half-open c-file.
notes.6: White's bishop aims at h7 and keeps your c8 bishop from coming to f5.
notes.7: Develop and add pressure on d4.
notes.8: White props up d4 with c3.
notes.9: Nf6 controls e4 and gets the king ready to castle.
notes.10: White develops the bishop outside the pawn chain.
notes.11: Get the bishop out actively before ...e6 locks it in. Watch out: with it gone from c8, b7 is loose and Qb3 hits it.
notes.12: Qb3 attacks b7. Defend it with ...Qd7, or hit the queen with ...Na5.

lines.name: Classical (4...Bf5)
lines.intro: In the Classical, you trade on e4 and develop your bishop to f5 with tempo. White chases it with Ng3 and h4–h5, you drop it back to g6 and then h7, and you keep a rock-solid position.

notes.0: White opens with the king's pawn.
notes.1: ...c6 prepares ...d5 and keeps the c8 bishop's diagonal open.
notes.4: White defends e4 with the knight instead of pushing or trading.
notes.5: Give up the center for now in exchange for fast, easy development.
notes.6: White takes back with the knight, which now sits in the center.
notes.7: Develop the bishop with tempo on the e4 knight.
notes.9: Keep the bishop on the diagonal. It retreats but doesn't go passive.
notes.10: White threatens h5 to trap your bishop.
notes.11: ...h6 makes room so the bishop can go to h7 when h5 comes.
notes.13: Nd7 stops White's Ne5 from hitting g6.
notes.14: White pushes on and attacks the bishop again.
notes.15: The bishop is safe on h7 and still aims at White's queenside.
